thread.title_full: Two CWU students awarded scholarships for study abroad programs in Hungary and South Korea

author: evergreen reporter
title: Two CWU students awarded scholarships for study abroad programs in Hungary and South Korea
text:
Two Central Washington University students will be studying abroad over the next year thanks to a pair of competitive scholarship awards, according to a June 17 announcement from the university.
Tess Ellsworth received the Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship from the U.S. Department of State and will spend the fall semester at the University of Pécs in Hungary. Another student, Ayla Lee, was awarded the Freeman-ASIA scholarship, which will fund her stay in South Korea from March to December 2027.
Ellsworth, who recently completed her third year at CWU and is pursuing dual degrees in psychology and business, said she sought help from the Office of International Studies and Programs (OISP) when she realized affording a study abroad opportunity would be difficult. “I went to OISP for an exploratory meeting about study abroad, and I was very up front that I didn’t have a lot of money to pay for it,” Ellsworth said. “They told me about a number of scholarship opportunities, so I applied for as many as I could.”
The Gilman Program provides up to $5,000 in merit-based scholarships to outstanding American undergraduate students with high financial need to pursue credit-bearing academic studies and career-oriented internships abroad. Ellsworth has been saving money from her job as a psychology tutor in the Learning Commons and plans to work with CWU Custodial Services this summer. She said receiving the Gilman Scholarship made her plans possible: “I submitted the application back in February, and I wasn’t sure what would happen,” she said. “But then I got an email telling me to check my Gilman account, and there was a new page saying I had received a scholarship. I was completely elated because without it, I didn’t know if I would be able to go.”
Lee will prepare during fall and winter quarters before beginning her Freeman-ASIA funded program next March. The Asian Studies major learned about potential scholarships through OISP staff members who informed her about Freeman-ASIA’s mission supporting U.S. undergraduates with demonstrated financial need studying in East or Southeast Asia.
“I have always been interested in South Korean culture and language, and I want to learn to speak Korean fluently,” Lee said. “I also hope that I can someday live in South Korea or be able to travel there more often.”
Both students hope their experiences overseas will broaden their perspectives academically and personally.
